+# Invention dossier: Proof-Carrying, Gate-First Polyintelligence Router
+
+Mechanism Recombination Foundry output for the GREG Polyintelligence Cortex seed. Machine-readable record:
+[`invention.json`](invention.json) (passes the Foundry's `validate_invention.py`). Patent or legal novelty is not
+claimed; this is an invention analysis, not legal advice.
+
+## The invention
+
+A router that answers each question from the mechanism with **legitimate epistemic jurisdiction** over it, makes
+that mechanism **prove its answer in that jurisdiction's terms**, **refuses or hands off** with a named missing fact
+when no mechanism may answer, sends **human-led protective actions to humans**, and lets its record of which
+mechanism works where **learn only from verified reality** — with no path by which competence, proof or
+confidence becomes authority.
+
+## 1. Why it is different
+
+| Existing system | What it does | What it cannot do that this does |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| LLM routers (RouterBench, LLMRouterBench) | pick the model with the best expected quality per cost | refuse with jurisdiction; check gates before ranking; emit class-specific proof; keep learning away from permission |
+| Algorithm portfolios (SATzilla) | pick the fastest solver for an instance of one problem class | span classes (formal, estimation, causal, semantic); select *nobody* as a correct outcome |
+| LLM + solver (Logic-LM, SymbolLKG) | translate to a solver and refine on errors | verify the translation against obligations and requester witnesses; mark unverified premises; certify optimality independently |
+| Proof-carrying code (Necula 1997) | ships a machine-checked safety proof with code | carry proof for *cognitive claims*, split formal, empirical and authority validity, and refuse to let proof authorize |
+| Signed agent receipts (IETF/SCITT drafts, 2026) | attest that an agent did something | attest what cognition could *not* establish: falsifiers, missing information, strongest counterargument |
+
+## 2. Mechanism anatomy
+
+Mechanism cards (source → extracted causal machinery, branding discarded):
+
+- **Portfolio selection** — state: instance features; transition: features → predicted performance → choice; invariant
+  kept: per-instance choice. Discarded: single problem class, runtime as the only objective.
+- **Router settlement** — state: per-model quality/cost estimates; feedback: observed results update estimates.
+  Kept: better methods earn more work. Discarded: self-reported or benchmark-only settlement.
+- **Proof-carrying** — producer ships evidence; consumer checks before relying. Kept: check, do not trust.
+  Discarded: proof implies permission to run.
+- **Translate–solve–refine** — model formalizes; solver decides. Kept: exact reasoning delegated to solvers.
+  Discarded: trust in the model's formalization.
+- **Model–identify–estimate–refute** — causal claims need identification and refutation. Kept entirely; mutated so a
+  model-generated diagram can never be the identification basis.
+- **Receipts** — canonical, content-addressed records. Kept; purpose inverted from attesting actions to attesting
+  limits.
+- **Constitutional separation** — models propose, the Kernel authorizes. Kept as the hard outer boundary.
+
+## 3. Mutation lineage
+
+| Source | Operator | New behavior | Invariant kept | New failure introduced |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Portfolio | constraint inversion + role widening | selection across epistemic classes; abstention and handoff are first-class, credited outcomes | per-instance selection | a payload can mimic a geometry |
+| Proof-carrying code | authority decoupling | typed proof per epistemic class; formal / empirical / authority truth split; `authority_created: false` enforced by schema | consumer checks evidence | valid proof of an unfaithful encoding (mitigated by reverse translation, witnesses, `WORLD_UNVERIFIED`) |
+| LLM routers | incentive mutation | settlement only by verified, provenance-weighted outcomes; learning permutes eligible routes only | better methods get more work | slow learning when outcomes are rare |
+| Hard constraints | sequencing inversion | gates over provenance-checked permission records before any ranking; Pareto front, not a scalar | best among feasible | over-blocking, surfaced as `UNRESOLVED` with a named resolution |
+| Signed receipts | purpose inversion | receipts publish falsifiers, missing information, strongest counterargument; never identities | canonical auditable records | prose falsifiers are only as precise as their templates |
+| Translate–solve–refine | verification insertion | reverse translation, obligation coverage, witnesses, counterexample search; undecided witness stops; optimality certificate | solver does exact reasoning | structural coverage cannot prove completeness |
+
+Every mutation that matters changes authority, incentives or consequences, not only implementation. None reduces
+to "use X with Y".
+
+## 4. System topology
+
+```
+question + structured facts
+  → geometry (epistemic class, consequence vector, reversibility, unknowns explicit)
+  → eligibility (Capability Genome may_instantiate, contraindications, light-cone ceiling)
+  → hard gates over permission-bearing records (when options exist)  ── fail → never ranked
+  → budget
+  → route or bounded composition (Semantic | Fermi | Formal/Optimization | Evidence/Causal)
+  → typed proof artifact
+  → model-free adversarial verifier (can only lower)
+  → recommend | bounded test | abstain | handoff  (human-led protection forces handoff)
+  → receipt (truth split, accountability, authority_created=false)
+  → Kernel policy engine → capability grant → Consequence Gate   (outside the cortex)
+  → outcome → competence ledger (verified only; permute eligible only; rollback)
+```
+
+## 5. Emergent behavior
+
+The interaction produces capabilities no source has alone:
+
+- **Jurisdictional refusal**: the system can say "no mechanism here may answer this; this is what is missing", and
+  that answer scores as correct.
+- **Disputes narrowed by construction**: every answer names the assumption, premise or observation that would
+  falsify it, so disagreement attacks evidence rather than the AI.
+- **Competence without sovereignty**: the routing record compounds from reality while being structurally unable to
+  widen permissions, ceilings or evaluators.
+- **Protection without exposure**: protective actions are ordered and handed to humans, and the audit trail proves
+  the handling without ever naming the person or channel.
+
+## 6. Incentive and authority design
+
+- Methods earn default routing per method × geometry × conditions × version, only from settled outcomes weighted by
+  validation status; predictions and self-assessments are refused as outcomes.
+- The scoring rule credits correct abstention (1.0) and penalizes confident error (0.0), with over-caution at 0.25,
+  so neither withholding nor bluffing wins.
+- Permission comes only from records whose kind and origin are verified (Kernel policy decision, founder-signed
+  mandate, Kernel grant, consent capture, qualified human legal opinion). Forged origins are rejected.
+- The cortex cannot import the Consequence Gate, adapters or any actuator; a static test enforces it.
+
+## 7. Omnidirectional effects
+
+| Party | Beneficial | Harmful or ambiguous | Redesign applied |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Founder | auditable answers; fewer opaque assertions; clear handoffs | more handoffs than a bluffing system | handoffs name the next step and missing fact |
+| Affected third parties / victims | protection routed to humans; identities never in receipts | cognition cannot act fast on their behalf | protection is ordered "protect now" first; human-led by design |
+| Operators | explicit states for every failure; reproducible freezes | more machinery than a single model | mutation check and traceability tests keep it honest |
+| Adversaries / counterparties | must attack named assumptions | a published falsifier is also a map of weak points | falsifiers name evidence to bring, which strengthens legitimate challenge |
+| Model vendors | swappable organs | lose lock-in | intended |
+| Future versions | contracts and reserved families give extension points | reserved names can look like capability | registry marks them disabled; register says "reserved" |
+| Second/third order | institutions can rely on bounded, falsifiable AI claims | over-trust in "proof" | truth split: formal ≠ empirical ≠ authority, on every receipt |
+
+## 8. Adversarial failure analysis
+
+- **Prompt injection in sources** → flagged by the verifier; the exact-quote check means injected text cannot
+  manufacture support.
+- **Forged permission records** → origin check per kind; mutation test proves a forged origin cannot grant.
+- **Evaluator gaming** → frozen suites by hash; held-out refuses changed inputs; evaluator-gaming items in the suite.

+- **Unfaithful formalization** → obligation coverage, requester witnesses, counterexample search,
+  `FORMALIZATION_INCOMPLETE`, `WORLD_UNVERIFIED`.
+- **Competence gaming** → only provenance-weighted verified outcomes settle; learning cannot touch the registry.
+- **Correlated agreement** → shared dependencies recorded; the verifier shares no model with any route.

+## 9. Novelty and precedent ledger
+
+| Element | Classification | Nearest precedent |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Per-instance routing | known primitive | SATzilla; RouterBench |
+| LLM-to-solver translation | known combination | Logic-LM; SymbolLKG Logic Router |
+| Proof shipped with output | known primitive (code) → mutated mechanism (cognition) | Necula 1997 |
+| Model → identify → estimate → refute | known implementation | DoWhy |
+| Signed canonical receipts | known implementation | IETF/SCITT agent-receipt drafts (2026) |
+| Abstention as a scored outcome | known primitive (selective prediction) | abstention surveys; AbstentionBench |
+| Gates over provenance-checked permission records *before* ranking, with Pareto tradeoffs | mutated mechanism | constrained optimization |

+| Outcome-only settlement that can permute eligible routes but never permissions | new authority relationship (likely) | routers learn routing; none located that structurally fences learning from authority |

+precedents; the likely novelty lies in the authority and proof relationships above. Strongest counterexample to the
+*value* claim: LLMRouterBench reports several routers, including a commercial one, failing to beat the best single
+model — so routing gain must be demonstrated, not assumed.

+# Polyintelligence Cortex — Seed Experiment
+
+The `cortex` package is the seed of GREG's Polyintelligence Cortex: a router that classifies a problem's
+geometry, checks which cognitive organs are eligible for it, runs the eligible ones under a budget, attacks
+their output with an independent verifier, and returns a recommendation, abstention, bounded test or handoff
+together with a content-addressed receipt.
+
+**Status:** cortex 0.2.1, converged onto GREG's mission path (`cognition.solve`, one registry, one receipt
+envelope, one settlement) · seven seed organs including a fault-diverse CP-SAT engine and the schedule-extraction
+composition · reserved families registered and disabled · **not promoted**. The frozen cross-geometry comparison
+against GREG's own baselines is reported in [`GREG_SEED_GENOME_REPORT.md`](GREG_SEED_GENOME_REPORT.md); the v0.1
+seed experiment is in [`SEED_EXPERIMENT_REPORT.md`](SEED_EXPERIMENT_REPORT.md).
+
+Source of requirements: the verbatim build prompt in
+[`docs/intent/sources/POLYINTELLIGENCE-CORTEX-BUILD-PROMPT-SEED-V0.1-2026-09-30.md`](../intent/sources/POLYINTELLIGENCE-CORTEX-BUILD-PROMPT-SEED-V0.1-2026-09-30.md).
+Every line of it is mapped to a status and evidence in [`BUILD_PROMPT_TRACEABILITY.json`](BUILD_PROMPT_TRACEABILITY.json),
+which `tests/unit/test_cortex_traceability.py` keeps honest. Every section of the two earlier AI review passes has a
+disposition in [`verbatim-register.json`](verbatim-register.json), checked by `tests/unit/test_cortex_register.py`.
+
+## Authority boundary
+
+Cognition creates no authority. Every receipt carries `authority_created: false` and
+`execution_authority: "none"`, enforced by its schema. The package cannot import the Consequence Gate, adapters
+or any actuator (`test_cortex_imports_nothing_that_can_act`). External consequences continue through the Kernel
+policy engine → capability grant → Consequence Gate. Financial and irreversible questions, legal, normative and
+institutional questions, and human-led victim-protection actions are handed off, never recommended.
+
+## Five layers
+
+The build prompt's five layers are a profile field (`profile.layer`) on each genome — selectable scales, not
+services. One process runs everything.
+
+| Layer (`profile.layer`) | Build prompt name | Enabled in the seed | Registered, disabled |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `primitive_basal` | Primitive / basal intelligence | — | feedback control, molecular micro-agents, anomaly patterning |
+| `distributed_collective` | Distributed / collective intelligence | — | ecology market, hive quorum, immune, slime network, stigmergy, swarm PSO, human panel |
+| `solver_macro_cognitive` | Solver / macro-cognitive intelligence | Semantic, Fermi, Formal (Z3, incl. certified optimization), Evidence/Causal, Deterrence | mechanism design, graph search, heuristic search, exact symbolic, CP-SAT, Bayesian, bandit, simulation twin |
+| `developmental_morphogenetic` | Developmental / morphogenetic intelligence | — | constraint release, evolutionary, MICA field, morphogenetic, program synthesis |
+| `meta_polyintelligence_cortex` | Meta-intelligence / Polyintelligence Cortex | adversarial verifier (and the router itself) | value of information, active inference, global workspace, mental models, metaconsensus |
+
+The earlier AI review used a different five-layer naming (L1–L5); `REVIEW_LAYER_MAP` in `cortex/contracts.py`
+reconciles the two and both are preserved. Every biological concept attached to a genome must name its
+mechanism, state variables, interface, feedback loop, measurable behavior, test and failure condition, or
+registration is refused.
+
+## Pipeline
+
+```
+problem → geometry → cognitive eligibility → budget → route or bounded composition
+        → typed artifact → adversarial verification → abstain / recommend / bounded test / handoff → receipt
+```
+
+Routing policy `cortex-route-policy/0.1` is deterministic: the structure of the payload selects routes
+(`formal_model` → Formal, `estimation_model` → Fermi, `claim` → Evidence/Causal, `sources` → Semantic). A model
+may *propose* geometry features through the `proposer` hook; a proposal is kept only when the structured payload
+supports it, and its confidence is recorded. When options are present, hard gates run before any ranking and
+ranking sees only options that passed every gate.
+
+## Routes
+
+| Organ | Mechanism | Proof class | Explicit non-OK states |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `cortex.semantic@0.1.0` | existing `egregore.local_model` client; only claims quoting an exact span of a cited source survive | `semantic_sourced` | `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE`, `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`, `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`, `MALFORMED_INPUT` |
+| `cortex.estimation.fermi@0.1.0` | unit-checked decomposition, Gaussian-copula Monte Carlo, sensitivity, reference class | `estimation` | `DIMENSION_MISMATCH`, `CONTESTED`, `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`, `MALFORMED_INPUT` |
+| `cortex.formal.z3@0.2.0` | requirement → model → reverse translation → discrepancy check → counterexample search → Z3 feasibility, entailment, or optimization with an independent UNSAT optimality certificate | `formal` | `FORMALIZATION_INCOMPLETE`, `WORLD_UNVERIFIED`, `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE`, `TIMEOUT`, `INCONCLUSIVE`, `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` |
+| `cortex.evidence_causal@0.1.0` | evidence rules (provenance, freshness, contradictions, missing observations); stratified/linear adjustment with bootstrap CI and refutations, only under declared identification | `evidence_assessment`, `causal_estimate` | `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`, `CONTESTED`, `NOT_IDENTIFIED`, `MALFORMED_INPUT` |
+| `cortex.deterrence.accountability@0.1.0` | Becker expected-value condition (gain − p_detect · p_sanction · sanction) over declared ranges; closed lawful intervention vocabulary; coercive and hard-harm interventions refused; levers labelled certainty / severity / opportunity; actions reaching another party handed off | `deterrence_assessment` | `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`, `MALFORMED_INPUT` |
+| `cortex.verifier.adversarial@0.1.0` | rule-based, model-free attack on artifacts and evidence; records shared dependencies | `verifier_findings` | findings only lower a disposition; a critical finding blocks `recommend` |
+
+## Receipts: truth, accountability, protection
+
+Every receipt separates **formal validity**, **empirical validity** and **legitimate authority**, and carries an
+**accountability** section: the strongest counterargument the verifier found, a falsification condition for each
+route's claim, and the missing information that would resolve the question. When victim protection is relevant,
+declared actions are ordered (protect now → preserve evidence → contain → safe contact → escalate → repair → prevent
+recurrence); unmeasured harm, unpreserved evidence, a missing safe channel or retaliation risk without disclosure
+controls are *gaps* that force a human handoff; and the receipt records only whether a person or safe channel was
+declared — never who or which.
+
+## Deterrence, lawfully
+
+Deterrence here means changing the expected value of misconduct for a risk-neutral actor (Becker 1968): misconduct
+pays when the gain exceeds detection probability × sanction probability × sanction. The organ samples the declared
+ranges, then ranks only interventions from a closed lawful vocabulary (detection, evidence preservation, access
+control, process change, independent audit, victim support; and, handed off to the competent authority, reporting,
+contractual remedies, transparency, restitution). Threats, retaliation, intimidation, extortion, deception, doxxing,
+unconsented surveillance, vigilantism, harassment and coercion are refused and never ranked. Each intervention is
+labelled by the lever it moves; a best option that moves only severity is flagged, because the evidence supports
+certainty of apprehension far more consistently (Nagin 2013).
+
+## Contracts
+
+JSON Schema 2020-12 in `contracts/`, validated strictly by `cortex/schemas.py` (deliberately not added to the
+shared-boundary allowlist):

+| Contract | Example (generated by a real run) |
+| --- | --- |
+| `cortex-problem-geometry` | [`examples/problem-geometry-formal.json`](examples/problem-geometry-formal.json) |
+| `cortex-intelligence-genome` | [`examples/genome-formal-z3.json`](examples/genome-formal-z3.json), [`examples/genome-reserved-disabled.json`](examples/genome-reserved-disabled.json) |
+| `cortex-proof-artifact` | [`examples/proof-formal.json`](examples/proof-formal.json), `proof-estimation`, `proof-evidence_assessment`, `proof-causal_estimate`, `proof-semantic_sourced` |
+| `cortex-receipt` | eleven receipts in [`examples/`](examples/), one per disposition path, incl. certified optimization, victim-protection handoff and deterrence (internal control recommended; report to authority handed off) |
+| `cortex-routing-memory` | [`examples/routing-memory-verified-success.json`](examples/routing-memory-verified-success.json) |
+
+Regenerate with `python -m cortex.examples --out docs/cortex/examples`. Receipts carry measured expenditure, so
+their ids change between runs; states and dispositions do not.
+

+

+**Freeze discipline.** Suites, scoring, arms, generators, route policy, organ code, budgets, partitions and
+thresholds are hashed into `cortex/evaluation/freeze-v<version>.json` before each reported run; the held-out run
+refuses if any input changed. Six versions were frozen and run; all manifests and results are kept.

Done before any declared baseline ran | traceability audit against item 11 |

+
+Held-out results were **identical item for item** across all six versions: no held-out item exercises the
+changed paths, and the exit change only matters once baselines run. That is a coverage gap, recorded under limitations; the paths are covered by unit and mutation tests.
+
+**Held-out results (cortex 0.1.5, `tests/evidence/cortex-seed-v0.1.5/heldout-results.json`):**

+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

+reference, not a declared baseline; this is not a routing-gain claim.

+Exit verdict: **`INCONCLUSIVE`, promote = false** — "declared baseline always_llm not run: configured local model
+unavailable", same for `llm_committee`.
+
+**Learning checks** (deterministic, on real receipts): absent and unresolved outcomes change nothing; a prediction
+offered as an outcome is refused; six externally verified successes move the Formal 0.1.1 cell from 0.50 to 0.97
+with the largest single update 0.28; rollback restores the prior state; the registry is unchanged.

+## Limitations
+
+1. **No routing-gain evidence.** The declared baselines did not run. Until they do, nothing here shows the routed
+   seed beats a strong LLM.
+2. **The held-out suite is self-authored.** The same agent wrote the routes and the items. Problems arrive as
+   structured payloads, so geometry derivation from free text is not tested. Treat 0.964 as an upper bound on
+   routing quality for structured intake, not as evidence about natural-language problems.
+3. **The Semantic organ has never run against a live model.** Its exact-quote check is tested with a scripted
+   client only.
+4. **Causal estimates use synthetic data** with planted effects. They show the estimator and its refusals work;
+   they say nothing about any real intervention.
+5. **Gold labels.** Formal golds were brute-force verified; the rest were labelled by the author.
+6. **Uncovered held-out paths.** Victim protection, solver timeouts and undecided witnesses have no held-out item.
+7. **No real outcomes.** The competence ledger is in memory and has settled zero real outcomes. "Compound
+   capability from reality" has its mechanism, not its evidence.
+8. **Small n.** 42 held-out items; confidence intervals are wide.
+9. **Rule-based verifier.** Prompt-injection detection is lexical; a paraphrase without trigger words passes. The

+# Spider-Web Hegemony — Executive brief: the Polyintelligence Cortex as GREG's cognition rail
+
+Profile: Executive. Scope: the cortex seed (cortex 0.1.5) treated as an evidence-gated market for cognition inside
+GREG — who may answer, who answers first, what counts as proof, and how competence settles. "Hegemony" here means
+legitimate control of that process through accepted proof and verified outcomes, never control over people and
+never authority beyond the Kernel's.
+
+## 1. Decision
+
+**Validate.** The architecture is coherent and built; its decisive commercial and strategic claims are unproven.
+Run the 90-day test below before any promotion or external use.
+
+## 2. Governing transaction
+
+- **Actor:** Alfonso, and GREG missions acting under his grants.
+- **Outcome:** a decision-grade answer to a mixed-geometry question (feasibility, optimization, estimate, causal
+  claim, sourced synthesis, choice among options) *before* a consequence is authorized.
+- **Broken governing state:** "which cognition may legitimately answer this, and what proves it". A single model
+  answers everything in one opaque voice; scope, falsifiers and authority are implicit; unanswerable questions get
+  answers anyway. (Verified fact: AbstentionBench reports reasoning models fail to abstain on unanswerable
+  questions; LLMRouterBench reports several routers fail to beat the best single model — so routing alone does not
+  fix this.)
+- **Boundary:** from question intake to the Kernel's authorization decision; execution is outside.
+- **Valid completion:** a receipt whose claim was produced by a mechanism with jurisdiction, carries typed proof and
+  falsifiers, creates no authority, and is later confirmed by a verified outcome — or a correct, named abstention
+  or handoff.
+
+## 3. Falsifiable thesis
+
+Become the accepted control layer for **GREG's pre-consequence cognition** by controlling **epistemic jurisdiction
+and proof class** at **the moment before the Kernel authorizes**, issuing **the cognitive receipt** (typed proof,
+truth split, falsifiers, `authority_created: false`), tied to **the Kernel's authorization and to outcome-settled
+competence**, while **single-model vendors** cannot copy it without **routing work away from their own model and
+publishing the falsifiers and abstentions that expose its errors**.
+
+Falsified if: against strong declared baselines the routed seed shows no per-geometry gain and no critical-error
+advantage on the frozen suite.
+
+## 4. Active Single Bottleneck Metric
+
+**Declared baselines run on the frozen held-out partition: 0 of 2 → 2 of 2**, then the exit verdict. Everything
+downstream waits on it.
+
+## 5. Strategic checksum (17)
+
+| # | Item | Status | Basis |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| 1 | Bounded failure | Pass | opaque single-model answers on mixed geometries; external evidence above; internal frequency unmeasured |
+| 2 | Mandate-capable actor | Pass | Alfonso is root authority and directed the build |
+| 3 | Accepted artifact | Unresolved | the cognitive receipt is issued; no consequential decision has accepted one yet |
+| 4 | Downstream consequence | Unresolved | by design receipts do not feed the Kernel's authorization yet (consequence-inert period) |
+| 5 | Eligibility mechanism | Pass | Capability Genome projection, contraindications, light-cone ceiling, hard gates |
+| 6 | Default-routing mechanism | Pass | deterministic structural policy; learned permutation of eligible routes only |
+| 7 | Proof-to-outcome mechanism | Unresolved | outcome link and settlement ledger built; zero settled outcomes |
+| 8 | NBOC trajectory | Unresolved | NBOC = accepted, outcome-verified receipts per decision routed; currently 0/0 |
+| 9 | Capital physics | Pass | local execution, $0 per decision, one optional dependency |
+| 10 | Incumbent self-harm constraint | Unresolved | real but weak: vendors bundle tools and code execution |
+| 11 | Four reinforcing loops | Unresolved | operational and institutional loops designed; capital and regenerative loops not measured |
+| 12 | Governance, succession, anti-entropy, kill criteria | Pass | founder authority, freeze discipline, mutation check, kill test |
+| 13 | Correct current business form | Pass | internal Tool; Platform and Operating System are premature |
+| 14 | Proprietary intelligence flywheel | Unresolved | workflow-created routing memory exists; no data |
+| 15 | Network effects | Not applicable | none claimed |
+| 16 | Five-outcome integrity | Fail (for Commit) | average 3.0; Commercial 1 |
+| 17 | Capital continuity proportional to stage | Not applicable | seed stage; no capital deployed |
+
+## 6. Correct business form
+
+- **Current:** Tool — an internal capability used by GREG under Kernel authority.
+- **Premature:** Platform or Operating System for third parties; any external "proof standard" claim.
+- **Transition evidence to Vertical Workflow:** `GAIN_VERIFIED` against a strong baseline on an externally authored
+  suite, then ≥ 50 shadow receipts on real GREG missions with zero authority assertions (backcast Node 2).
+
+## 7. Artifact and consequence
+
+- **Issuer:** the cortex. **Accepting authority:** Alfonso and the Kernel policy engine.
+- **Decision changed (target):** whether a mission step proceeds, abstains, runs a bounded test, or hands off.
+- **Current authority level:** informational only; consequence-inert by constitution.
+
+## 8. NBOC target
+
+Natural denominator: decisions routed through the cortex. NBOC = accepted, outcome-verified receipts ÷ decisions
+routed. Current 0/0. Month-6 target after VEPMC ≥ 1 and shadow use: ≥ 30 verified outcomes across ≥ 3 geometry cells
+with ≥ 5 weighted outcomes each (the ledger's evidence threshold).
+
+## 9. Five-outcome summary
+
+| Outcome | Score | Evidence | Decisive blocker |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Commercial | 1 | no use, no revenue, no external buyer; internal tool | no comparative proof, no real use |
+| Strategic | 3 | owns GREG's eligibility, routing, proof and settlement for cognition | unaccepted artifact; gain unproven |
+| Regenerative | 4 | abstention credited; victim protection human-led with identity-free receipts; harm vector unknown-by-default | protection paths untested on held-out items |
+| Institutional | 4 | authority separation enforced by schema and tests; frozen, disclosed versions; full traceability | no external audit |
+| Capital | 3 | near-zero marginal cost; model-vendor independence | no outcome data asset yet |
+| **Average** | **3.0** | | Commit requires ≥ 4 with none below 3 |
+
+## 10. Primary architecture
+
+- **Eligibility:** IntelligenceGenome projection of the Capability Genome; hard gates over provenance-checked
+  permission records (law, rights, founder scope, consent, evidence floor, harm, budget, consequence) before ranking.
+- **Default routing:** deterministic payload-structure policy; outcome-settled permutation among eligible routes
+  only, with a margin and evidence threshold.
+- **Proof / truth:** typed proof per epistemic class; formal / empirical / authority split; accountability section
+  (strongest counterargument, falsifiers, missing information); model-free verifier that can only lower.
+- **Settlement:** competence per method × geometry × conditions × version from verified outcomes only, weighted by
+  validation status; predictions and self-assessments refused; rollback.
+- **Intelligence conversion:** the routing memory is created by the workflow and changes three decisions: which
+  eligible route runs first; which reserved family to build next (frequency of `NO_ELIGIBLE_METHOD` and abstentions
+  by geometry); which evaluation items to add (failure families where routes disagree with outcomes). It never
+  changes permissions, ceilings or evaluators.
+
+## 11. Strongest counter-position and strongest failure
+
+- **Counter-position (against us):** a strong single model with code execution and tool calls, given the same
+  facts, matches the routed seed at lower engineering cost. LLMRouterBench's Best-Single result makes this the
+  default expectation.
+- **Our counter-position:** jurisdictional refusal, typed falsifiable proof and authority-free receipts are things a
+  vendor optimizing for answer volume has reason not to ship; the Kernel, not the vendor, owns authority.
+- **Strongest failure:** `GAIN_ABSENT` against the strong baseline. Then the router is retired as a performance claim
+  and survives only as a gate-and-receipt layer if it still reduces critical errors.
+
+## 12. 90-day test and next external action
+
+- **Buyer:** Alfonso (internal decision owner).
+- **Number changed:** declared baselines run 0/2 → 2/2; exit verdict recorded with per-geometry paired gains.
+- **Evidence:** results file against the committed freeze v0.1.5, both baselines `RUN`.
+- **Budget ceiling:** $0 with a local model; ≤ $5 for a frontier `always_llm` run, only on founder authorization;
+  ≤ 2 hours agent time per run.
+- **Deadline:** within 30 days of a reachable model; the 90-day window closes with a recorded verdict.
+- **Termination trigger:** `GAIN_ABSENT` against the strong baseline on two frozen versions with no critical-error
+  advantage.
+- **Next external action:** make a model reachable for the baselines (allow a model host in the environment's
+  network settings, or run the command on a machine with Ollama).
+
+## 13. Final command
+
+**Validate.**
+
+## Addendum, 2026-10-01: Stage-gate
+
+The cognitive substrate now runs on GREG's mission path and has a frozen comparison against GREG's own
+baselines (`docs/cortex/GREG_SEED_GENOME_REPORT.md`). It remains an internal competency substrate. No
+external actor has accepted its artifacts for a consequential transaction, so market control, mandates,
+capital effects and network effects are unproven.
+
+- **Decision: Stage-gate.**
+- **Next external action:** the founder selects a local model on Body 1, and the frozen v0.3 suite's
+  `always_llm` and `tool_llm` arms run.
+- **Number it must change:** model arms run 0/2 -> 2/2, with a recorded verdict against the strongest of
+  them.
+- **Evidence required:** results tied to `cortex/evaluation/freeze-crossgeo-v0.3.json`.
+- **Budget:** local model only; no paid inference without the founder's own signed selection.
+- **Termination trigger:** `GAIN_ABSENT` against the strongest model arm on two frozen versions with no
+  hard-failure advantage. In that case keep the static router as default and retain the cortex
+  mechanisms only where fault and adversarial evidence shows they earn their cost.
+

+# ADR: Adopt the GREG Polyintelligence Cortex seed as a SANDBOXED, unpromoted experiment
+
+- Decision ID: polyintelligence-cortex-20260930
+- Status: proposed
+- Date: 2026-10-01
+- Decision owner: Alfonso Lopez
+- Deliberation level: Constitutional (adds five names to the shared Kernel contract registry; creates no authority)
+- Founder intent references: PC-001 to PC-012 in

+  [`INTENT-20260930-polyintelligence-cortex`](../intent/INTENT-20260930-polyintelligence-cortex.json); INTENT-0030

+  (passes the protocol's `validate_deliberation.py`)
+- Supersedes: none
+- Superseded by: none
+
+## Problem
+
+- **Observation:** `main` (19fa33c) has no cognition routing; the Capability Genome, policy engine, causal memory and
+  Consequence Gate exist; no capability or model router is implemented (Final Build Order §4.14 lists one as unbuilt).
+- **Observation:** the founder's build prompt ordered a seed experiment; it is built on a draft branch as cortex 0.1.5.
+- **Inference:** single-model answers on mixed geometries lack jurisdiction, typed proof and gates; whether routing
+  beats a strong single model is unknown.
+- **Unresolved claim:** routing gain. The declared baselines have not run.
+- **Proposed action:** merge as a SANDBOXED, consequence-inert experiment after founder review; promote only on
+  `GAIN_VERIFIED`.
+
+## Baseline and evidence
+
+| Claim | Claim class | Evidence tier | Source and location | Finding | Limitation |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Routed seed quality | observation | deterministic fixture | `tests/evidence/cortex-seed-v0.1.5/heldout-results.json` | 0.964 [0.911, 1.000]; 0 critical errors | self-authored, structured items |

+| Safeguards load-bearing | implementation | unit test | `scripts/ci/check_cortex_mutants.py` | 26/26 mutants caught | mutants are hand-chosen |
+| Stacks on PR #137 | observation | sandbox execution | report § Stacking on PR #137 | clean merge at `71b6f74`; 1570 vs 1201 passed, same 12 skips | isolated venv; PR #137 may move |
+| Best Single is hard to beat | external evidence | primary source | LLMRouterBench (arXiv 2601.07206) | several routers fail to beat it | different task mix |
+
+## Alternatives
+
+- **Current baseline:** no cortex on `main`.
+- **Do nothing:** branch stays a draft. Zero change to `main`; primitives drift; the directive stays off `main`.
+- **Simplest viable alternative:** gate-and-receipt layer around one model, without exact organs. Kept as the fallback.
+- **Strongest competing architecture:** a strong single model with tools. It is the declared baseline to beat.
+- **Reversible experiment:** merge SANDBOXED and consequence-inert; revert is one merge revert.
+
+Rejected: the full 16-family cortex now (revive on `GAIN_VERIFIED` plus recorded deficits); promotion on the 0.964
+result (revive on `GAIN_VERIFIED` on an external suite against strong baselines).
+
+## Five-role review
+
+| Role | Position | Material concerns | Evidence | Recommendation |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

+- Approver: none yet.
+
+## Decision
+
+`NEEDS_FOUNDER_DECISION` — the five roles recommend `EXPERIMENT` (merge SANDBOXED, unpromoted); the merge itself is
+Alfonso's decision.
+
+## Migration, rollback, and kill criteria
+

+- **Rollback:** revert the merge commit (removes the cortex, its five registry names and CI job 6 together).
+- **Kill criteria:** `GAIN_ABSENT` against strong baselines on two frozen versions with no critical-error advantage;

+## Problem

+For empirical and causal claims, assess provenance, measurements, identification assumptions, bias, sensitivity, and counterevidence. Refutation tests can expose problems; passing them does not prove the causal model correct.
+
+For values, consent, rights, disputed legal applicability, or institutional adjudication, route to the authorized human/policy process where required. Evidence collection may continue within existing authority.
+
+Support explicit outcomes:
+ANSWERED_WITHIN_SCOPE; CONDITIONAL_RESULT; ABSTAIN; WAIT; REQUEST_EVIDENCE; SMALL_EXPERIMENT; ESCALATE.
+
+Support machine-readable reasons, including:
+UNKNOWN_GEOMETRY; NO_ELIGIBLE_METHOD; INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE; WORLD_UNVERIFIED; NON_IDENTIFIABLE; FORMALIZATION_INCOMPLETE; MODEL_INVALID; SOLVER_UNKNOWN; TIMEOUT; BUDGET_EXHAUSTED; CONTRADICTION; OUT_OF_DISTRIBUTION; HUMAN_JUDGMENT_REQUIRED; AUTHORITY_REQUIRED; POLICY_REFUSAL; CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE.
+
+Map these into existing project statuses. Do not let a new taxonomy break consumers.
+
+7. IMPLEMENT THE SEED, END TO END
+
+Build four bounded competency classes and one independent verifier through existing runtime seams. Supply real executable mechanisms and narrow declared scopes.
+
+A. Semantic.
+Use the existing authorized local-model adapter for interpretation, synthesis, hypothesis generation, explanation, and structured drafts. Bind claims to actual retrieved evidence; distinguish proposed ideas from factual claims. Validate outputs. Record model identity, version, limits, and observed cost. If no permitted model is available, return CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE; fixtures remain fixtures.
+
+B. Estimation.
+Execute dimensional checks and numeric calculations outside the language model. Return decomposition, units, assumptions, ranges, dependencies, inside/outside-view anchors where available, sensitivity, dominant uncertainty, and the cheapest decision-changing information. Distinguish scenario bounds from statistically justified intervals. Reject invented precision, unsupported independence assumptions, and fabricated anchors.
+
+C. Formal/Optimization.
+Keep separate adapters behind the shared competency envelope.
+Formal: use a maintained SMT solver such as Z3 for an explicitly bounded feasibility/invariant domain. Preserve SAT, UNSAT, and UNKNOWN; distinguish a model from a proof, and a returned unsat core from a minimal or independently verified certificate.
+Optimization: use an appropriate maintained solver, such as OR-Tools CP-SAT for a bounded discrete scheduling/allocation domain. Preserve native statuses, objective direction/value, feasibility, bound/gap where available, timeout, and resource limits. Check the returned assignment independently against source constraints. FEASIBLE is not OPTIMAL.
+Use a declarative restricted input model. Do not execute arbitrary model-generated Python as formalization. Reverse translation supports review but cannot be the only validator.
+
+D. Evidence/Causal.
+Implement claim-evidence binding, source quality/freshness, contradictory-evidence handling, and explicit causal routing.
+For the first causal estimator, choose one narrowly identified domain with a checked statistical implementation, such as a specified randomized two-arm experiment or a well-defined adjustment example. Include treatment, outcome, population, estimand, assumptions, missingness/selection limits, uncertainty, sensitivity/refutation, and scope.
+Demonstrate one identifiable synthetic case against known ground truth and one non-identifiable or inadequately evidenced case that abstains. Label synthetic evidence. General causal inference remains a scoped expansion.
+An agent that merely asks an LLM for a DAG is not an implemented causal organ.
+
+E. Independent adversarial verifier.
+Run relevant deterministic and failure-diverse checks: arithmetic/units, constraint satisfaction, evidence mismatch, material omission, contradiction, source contamination, authority mismatch, and counterexamples. Add model critique only when it supplies measurable value.
+The verifier can invalidate or escalate a result within the existing evaluation contract. It cannot authorize an action. Preserve dissent and unresolved uncertainty.
+
+Provide at least one seed composition that executes across real heterogeneous mechanisms. For example: semantic extraction of a bounded scheduling request, validated declarative constraints, optimization, independent constraint checking, typed receipt, and existing authority handoff. Keep objective correctness checks independent of the extractor.
+
+Route local freshness, signatures, schema validity, budgets, and primitive state checks through L1. Give active capabilities bounded L2 profiles. This makes all five scales architecturally representable without claiming every future L4 mechanism has been built.
+
+8. IMPLEMENT ELIGIBILITY, ROUTING, COMPOSITION, AND METACONSENSUS
+
+Start with a deterministic, inspectable router over validated problem features. A classifier may propose geometry; it cannot lower the consequence class, remove material conditions, or create eligibility. Route mixed questions by subclaim. Preserve uncertainty about classification.
+
+Before ranking methods, enforce hard eligibility:
+supported geometry; adequate evidence; compatible proof class; allowed data use; tested version; health; available resources; valid grants; consequence ceiling; privacy; dependency availability; and absence of contraindications.
+
+An ineligible method must never win through a high score. A catalog entry is not eligibility. Model self-confidence is not measured competence.
+
+Among eligible methods, prefer the lowest expected total cost that meets the required quality, evidence, latency, and risk thresholds. Include classification, translation, verification, retries, tool overhead, maintenance burden, and founder attention. Keep objectives and weights versioned and inspectable. Use abstention when no eligible route satisfies the contract.
+
+The operating cycle is:
+observe discrepancy; decompose claims; classify epistemology and geometry; establish the competence/permission envelope; determine eligible methods; allocate a bounded cognitive budget; route or compose; obtain independent first-pass results where needed; collect typed artifacts; falsify and verify; reconcile by epistemic jurisdiction; emit a recommendation, experiment proposal, evidence request, or abstention; use the existing authority path for any consequence; observe the outcome; settle conditional competence; revise future routing.
+
+All resource use, external retrieval, model calls, and data access remain subject to existing grants before invocation. The final consequence check is not the first permission check.
+
+Composition rules:
+- Prefer the smallest sufficient composition.
+- Define typed inputs, outputs, assumptions, data scope, and failure propagation at each edge.
+- Do not convert a confidence score into a proof certificate.
+- Do not silently convert a formal conclusion into an empirical fact.
+- Preserve separate first-pass results before information exchange when independence matters.
+- Bound message volume, iterations, time, and resources.
+- Detect correlated errors and shared source dependencies.
+- Preserve material minority findings and unresolved contradictions.
+- Require measured marginal value over a simpler pipeline.
+
+Metaconsensus must reconcile claims rather than average incompatible answers. For each result, ask what question it answered, under which assumptions, with what proof type and scope. A causal non-identifiability finding is not outvoted by semantic plausibility. A violated feasibility condition cannot be averaged with enthusiasm. Human authority settles legitimate judgment within its scope, not empirical truth by decree.
+
+Return the next cheapest decisive test when disagreement can be resolved. Otherwise preserve the disagreement and abstain or escalate.
+
+Mental models must change the representation or decision: first principles, inversion, reference classes, Fermi decomposition, Bayesian updating, expected value, opportunity cost, regret, Pareto and power-law analysis, weakest-link analysis, fat tails, option value, second/third-order effects, path dependence, reversible decisions, counter-positioning, buyer/payer/gatekeeper analysis, proof and control-point analysis, moat paths, risk transfer, constraint recombination, and ethical legitimacy. Record the transformation and its usefulness rather than printing a checklist.
+
+9. PROOF-CARRYING COGNITION AND CHALLENGE-RESISTANT RECORDS
+
+Implement proof artifacts appropriate to the claim:
+
+Claim/method | Required artifact
+Exact arithmetic/symbolic | Typed inputs, units, exact or bounded arithmetic, executable expression, result, independent check where warranted.
+Formal | Formal statement/model, assumptions, constraints, solver/version/options, native status, model/counterexample, proof or core where supported, verification limits.
+Optimization | Objective, constraints, assignment, feasibility check, native status, bound/gap if available, budget, and timeout.
+Estimation | Decomposition, references, assumptions, dependencies, ranges, sensitivity, dominant uncertainty.
+Probabilistic/prediction | Data scope, priors/likelihood or predictive model, posterior/forecast, diagnostics, calibration and validation context.
+Causal | Estimand, causal model, identification assumptions, data, estimator, uncertainty, confounders, sensitivity/refutation, non-identifiability where applicable.
+Semantic | Claim-source mapping, provenance, material contradictions, interpretation boundaries, uncertainty.
+Simulation | Simulator/version, model assumptions, calibration evidence, scenario design, seeds, output distribution, failure cases, domain of validity.
+Control | Plant/model scope, observations and estimator, set-points, limits, controller settings, stability/safety assumptions, observed trajectory.
+Human | Verified role where required, scope, deliverable, evidence, conflicts, dissent, and separate authority reference.
+Institutional acceptance | Named accepting actor, actual response/action, applicable terms or process, scope, date, and revocation/appeal path.
+
+Use one receipt envelope with a typed artifact union. Extend it for future families. An unsupported proof type is a validation failure.
+
+For accountable external use, produce a selective-disclosure evidence package: observations, provenance, chain of custody, assumptions, formal results, empirical limitations, conflicting evidence, requested remedy, and authorized action record. Protect raw sensitive evidence under existing retention and access rules.
+
+An institution may dispute the data, model, jurisdiction, completeness, or relevance, and may decline a proposed action. Record that response. Do not claim proof compels acceptance.
+
+10. BUILD THE COGNITIVE SPIDER-WEB INSIDE EXISTING GOVERNANCE
+
+The bounded transaction is: a GREG mission needs a justified cognitive result, but completion fails when method selection, evidence type, or outcome attribution is wrong.
+
+Implement the four connected mechanisms:
+Eligibility: independently supported method competence under task-specific conditions.
+Default routing: the cheapest sufficient eligible method, with explicit escalation.
+Proof/truth: typed artifacts with checks appropriate to the claim.
+Settlement: observed outcomes update geometry-specific competence, calibration, cost, latency, and contraindications.
+
+Settlement means accountable outcome reconciliation here. Do not invent a token economy, financial exchange, or new payment authority.
+
+Apply the eight Spider-Web sides proportionately:
+1. Failure geometry: measure wrong-method selection, invalid claims, and unresolved work.
+2. Participant geometry: identify founder, mission owner, affected people, operators, evaluators, data subjects, and external accepting actors.
+3. Eligibility: publish inspectable qualification and exclusion reasons.
+4. Routing: select and explain defaults while preserving approved alternatives.
+5. Proof: bind claims to evidence and enable challenge and correction.
+6. Settlement: reconcile results without duplicating credit or authority.
+7. Adoption: attach to the existing GREG path; demonstrate user value before claiming institutional reliance.
+8. Continuity: fund resource ceilings, recovery, retention, appeal, and revocation.
+
+Evaluate the operational loop, resource-efficiency loop, trust/acceptance loop, and participant-benefit loop separately. Measure delays, failure modes, and saturation. Do not call data accumulation a network effect or an internal receipt an external standard.
+
+Track benefits to eligibility, routing, and verification decisions before claiming a proprietary cognitive learning advantage. Any later business advantage must also show externally accepted outcomes and positive participant economics.
+
+11. CONNECT OUTCOMES TO ONE LEARNING PLANE
+
+Extend existing causal memory and learning infrastructure. Represent:
+problem; claim; input conditions; method/version; recommendation/prediction; artifact; authorization; action; outcome; observation provenance; time delay; cost; error; calibration; contribution hypotheses; update.
+
+Index competence by method x geometry x conditions x version. Retain sample counts, uncertainty, failures, missing outcomes, and domain shift. A universal superiority badge is prohibited.
+
+Keep distinct:
+- validated benchmark outcomes;
+- simulated or synthetic outcomes;
+- observed real-world outcomes;
+- independently verified outcomes;
+- commercial and participant outcomes.
+
+Offline benchmark evidence may inform a sandbox routing policy. It cannot masquerade as deployment evidence. Real-outcome updates require authentic observations and appropriate validation. Missing, delayed, censored, or confounded outcomes must not be scored as success.
+
+Settlement must be idempotent, versioned, attributable, and correctable. Corrections append a superseding record rather than silently rewriting history. Keep personal-data handling compatible with lawful retention and deletion requirements.
+
+Attribute contributions to hypothesis generation, error detection, uncertainty reduction, cost, and failed assumptions. Unless a defensible causal design supports stronger language, call this contribution attribution, not proven causal credit.
+
+Begin with deterministic routing and an auditable competence ledger. Add learned routing only after adequate data and held-out evidence. Use shadow/champion-challenger comparison, drift checks, rollback, exploration ceilings, and protection for rare but valuable methods. Do not punish a method for appropriate abstention.
+
+For future bandits, record selection propensities, eligible alternatives, delayed feedback, and policy versions where required for valid evaluation. Use learning only over already permitted choices. A reward model never grants a new choice.
+
+Offline consolidation may replay, compress, cluster, detect contradictions, extract abstractions, and propose experiments. Preserve provenance, uncertainty, and falsifying cases. Generated hypotheses remain provisional.
+
+12. MAKE COGNITIVE EXPENDITURE DECISION-AWARE
+
+Build a bounded thinking-budget controller using existing budget infrastructure.
+
+Before optional deeper cognition, estimate whether another calculation, model call, simulation, lookup, or founder interruption could change the decision enough to justify its total cost. Use ranges when the estimate is uncertain. Log the stopping reason.
+
+Value of information concerns improved decisions; entropy reduction alone is insufficient. Cheap irrelevant information has little decision value.
+
+Mandatory verification and permission checks are not optional costs to optimize away. If the remaining budget cannot support the required evidence, return a narrower conditional result, request evidence, wait, or abstain.
+
+Track latency distributions and tail behavior, not just mean cost. Count local CPU/RAM/storage and energy when measurable; zero token fees do not imply free or unbounded computation.
+
+Founder attention is a scarce resource, but necessary human judgment must remain reachable. Escalations state the exact decision, evidence, options, costs, uncertainty, authority needed, and consequences of waiting. Do not manufacture urgency or frame refusal as harming GREG.
+
+13. OPERATIONALIZE LAWFUL ASYMMETRIC ADVANTAGE
+
+For each consequential proposal, produce an inspectable AdvantageCase:
+desired outcome; bounded failure; beneficiaries; affected parties; existing authority; lawful options; do-nothing/smallest-intervention options; evidence; control point; expected benefit; uncertainty; reusable assets; dependencies; consequence vector; reversibility; resource burden; strongest counterexample; minimum test; stop conditions.
+
+Optimize within hard constraints, then compare a Pareto frontier of defensible alternatives. Prefer the strongest lawful option whose expected benefit, evidence, durability, and optionality justify its residual exposure.
+
+Do not implement the supplied multiplicative leverage formula as a scientifically validated score. Its terms have different units, uncertain dependence, and potentially unstable denominators. If a score assists ranking, specify normalization, weights, sensitivity, missingness, and policy ownership. Keep hard prohibitions outside the score.
+
+Do not represent legality, consent, rights, or authority as unsupported Law = 1 assertions. Use applicable evidence-backed states such as supported, prohibited, unresolved, and not applicable, with jurisdiction/scope, provenance, expiry, and reviewer when required. Lack of a detected prohibition is not permission.
+
+Implement these six outcomes individually:
+Evidence: provenance, completeness, contradiction preservation, independent checks, defensible custody, and correction.
+Institutional leverage: identify the actual accepting/deciding actor, applicable process, accepted artifact, and decision it can legitimately change.
+Accountability: attributable decisions, traceable duties, explanation, appeal, error correction, restitution where applicable, and preserved failures.
+Deterrence: reduce exploitable opportunity and expected payoff through lawful access controls, reliable detection, durable evidence, appropriate process, and recurrence prevention.
+Victim protection: contain immediate and continuing harm, protect evidence and privacy, account for retaliation, and route necessary support through authorized channels.
+Minimal collateral harm: enforce rights/safety constraints first, then minimize each remaining exposure without hiding it in a single scalar.
+
+For protection cases, use:
+affected_party; immediate_harm; continuing_harm; retaliation_risk; privacy_risk; financial_harm; reputational_harm; rights_impact; evidence_at_risk; safe_contact_channel; required_authority; applicable_notification_duties; containment_options; investigation_scope; restitution_options; recurrence_controls.
+
+Apply proportionate sequencing: protect, preserve, contain, investigate, escalate, repair, prevent recurrence. The exact ordering depends on immediate danger and lawful duties. Route professional decisions to qualified people.
+
+Deterrence models may examine actor incentives, opportunity, detection, evidence durability, accountability, and repeatability. Never turn "reduce anonymity" into unauthorized identification, doxxing, indiscriminate surveillance, or exposure of vulnerable people. No threats, harassment, sabotage, deception, retaliation, or corrupt institutional influence.
+
+Durable business leverage must make participants more capable, trusted, eligible, and easier to transact with. Test value distribution, hidden burden transfer, consent, privacy, exit, appeal, and lawful competition. Commercial success cannot depend on preserving the underlying harm.
+
+Use evidence to earn default routing and acceptance. Keep interoperability and replaceability. Do not manufacture lock-in, standards recognition, market inevitability, or dominance claims.
+
+14. DISTINGUISH ROBUSTNESS, RESILIENCE, AND ANTIFRAGILITY
+
+Robustness: specified disturbances do not materially violate the service contract.
+Resilience: after specified damage, the system restores the authorized function within measured recovery limits.
+Antifragility: bounded stress, coupled to a verified learning mechanism, produces a subsequent measurable improvement relative to an appropriate control, after counting stress and repair costs.
+Durable compounding: retained improvements continue delivering value over repeated workloads without eroding rights, authority, reliability, or resources.
+
+These are scoped empirical claims. Do not guarantee perpetual improvement or benefit from every shock.
+
+Implement and measure:
+- process interruption and restart with durable state;
+- replay-safe receipt and outcome settlement;
+- provider/method failure and graceful degradation;
+- invalid/stale evidence and revocation;
+- corrupted artifacts and dependency failures;
+- timeouts, memory pressure, exhausted budgets, and unavailable models;
+- divergent or conflicting state across bodies;
+- restoration from retained evidence and tested backups;
+- controlled regression to a simpler working method;
+- fault-diverse alternatives for critical functions.
+
+Use existing durable execution and event infrastructure. Git may version source and artifacts; it does not roll back real-world consequences or automatically establish causation. No bespoke database, blockchain, network stack, hypervisor, or operating system without a demonstrated residual deficit and approved scope.
+
+Persistent goal pursuit uses bounded tasks, scheduled events, backoff, and durable waits. It does not require continuous model calls or infinite retry. Preserve authorized objectives across interruptions; replan means using new evidence within the mission contract. Material goal changes, expanded budgets, and renewed authority follow the existing human/policy path.
+
+Choose recovery-time, recovery-point, detection, containment, duplicate-effect, and authority-continuity thresholds before testing. State the environment and failures covered. One logical authority can have resilient infrastructure; multiple copies must not become competing policy authorities. Unresolved authority conflict blocks new consequences.
+
+For uncertain external completion, reconcile with the external system before retrying. Idempotency and durable deduplication require adapter-specific contracts. Do not claim universal exactly-once effects across arbitrary services.
+
+The immune mechanism detects anomalies, challenges evidence, narrows coupling, quarantines within existing authority, preserves forensics, repairs, verifies, and cautiously recouples. Test false positives, false negatives, and wrongful quarantine. Unfamiliarity alone is not an attack.
+
+Use bounded sandbox disturbances to test antifragility. Freeze an untouched holdout and compare the improved system against its pre-stress version and a no-learning control. Count damage, recovery costs, latency, and regressions. Reject improvement caused by test leakage or evaluator weakening.
+
+Preserve continuity by making legitimate shutdown effective. Every recovery and failover test must include revocation persistence.
+
+15. FREEZE THE EVALUATION BEFORE OPTIMIZING TO IT
+
+The cognition bottleneck is Verified Cross-Geometry Routing Gain. Method count, agent count, model size, code volume, and test count are not substitutes.
+
+Define normalized per-task loss before observing candidate results. It must include outcome error, false claims, unjustified abstention, calibrated uncertainty where meaningful, total cost, latency, and task-specific failure. Safety and authority violations remain separate hard failures. Publish units, weights, aggregation, and per-stratum results.
+
+Routing gain = expected loss of the strongest relevant deployable baseline minus expected loss of the routed system, measured on the same held-out workload and resource envelope.
+
+Routing regret compares selected performance with the best eligible method for that instance. A hindsight oracle is an evaluation reference, not a deployable system or proof of a route the agent could have selected in advance.
+
+Compare:
+1. The existing GREG path, without the new cortex.
+2. A documented always-LLM baseline.
+3. The strongest permitted tool-enabled model/workflow baseline with equivalent data, tools, and budget.
+4. A simple static rules-based specialist router.
+5. The proposed router or composition.
+
+For later learned routing, compare against the frozen static router. For collective cognition, compare against the strongest constituent, a simple pipeline, and an ordinary agent committee. Use legally and operationally available baselines; do not incur unapproved provider costs to satisfy a comparison.
+
+Create a frozen seed suite covering:
+- source-grounded semantic synthesis and proposed strategy;
+- estimation with units, ranges, dependencies, and uncertainty;
+- satisfiable, unsatisfiable, and bounded-unknown formal problems;
+- feasible/infeasible scheduling and optimization;
+- identified synthetic causal effects and non-identifiable claims;
+- mixed, ambiguous, unknown-geometry, missing-evidence, rights-sensitive, and abstention cases.
+
+Use multiple independent problem families and held-out transformations, not three showcase examples. As an initial engineering coverage floor, supply 20 held-out cases per listed stratum plus a separate adversarial suite. This floor is a design requirement, not a statistical sufficiency claim. Determine the sample size needed to resolve the predeclared material effect; report inconclusive when budget prevents it.
+
+Separate development, selection, and held-out evaluation. Freeze generator versions, input digests, labels, scoring, budgets, stopping criteria, and permitted exclusions. Do not expose answers or oracle method labels to the router. Keep related templates and paraphrases in the same split to avoid leakage.
+
+Use exact evaluators where possible. For open-ended quality, use explicit rubrics, blinded evaluation where available, and disclosed evaluator limitations. A model grading its own output does not establish superiority. Repeat stochastic runs and report uncertainty without counting repeated outputs from one problem as independent tasks.
+
+Make the frozen benchmark runner fully automated, with no human intervention during runs. Any expert annotation, scope decisions, and rubric design occur before freezing. Human/external acceptance is evaluated separately when it is itself the required real-world outcome; a simulated reviewer cannot satisfy that outcome.
+
+Predeclare the smallest practically meaningful gain. A proposed default is a 10% reduction in the predeclared aggregate loss against the strongest relevant baseline, with the lower bound of an appropriate 95% confidence interval above zero and no unacceptable regression in any critical stratum. Change this target only before the final evaluation, with a recorded rationale. Do not tune weights after seeing results.
+
+Mandatory release evidence:
+- all required authority and isolation checks pass;
+- every completed evaluation case has a valid typed receipt;
+- all statuses and abstentions preserve their meanings;
+- the required real solver and computation paths execute;
+- restart/replay and revocation tests meet their declared contracts;
+- no hidden paid fallback or unauthorized external effect occurs;
+- source-backed claims survive the independent checks;
+- the benchmark report contains all failures and inconclusive results.
+
+Mandatory adversarial cases:
+misclassified high-consequence problem; omitted material constraint; contradiction; dimensional error; misleading source; stale evidence; forged artifact; prompt injection in retrieved text; false proof type; unsupported confidence; solver timeout/UNKNOWN; invalid optimization model; non-identifiable causal question; missing human authority; duplicate outcome delivery; replayed approval; revoked grant after restart; unavailable model; resource exhaustion; wrong model provenance; correlated verifier error; contaminated evaluation; and a proposal that improves a scalar score by harming a protected party.
+
+Use mutation tests for critical gates: deliberately remove a permission check, drop a constraint, relabel UNKNOWN, replace evidence, duplicate settlement, or enable a paid fallback. The corresponding tests must fail. This validates the gates rather than merely matching implementation details.
+
+If routing gain is absent, preserve the negative result and retain the strongest simpler implementation. Diagnose the failure and conduct the next bounded test within budget. Do not relabel a failed advantage experiment as a proven cortex.
+
+16. CONNECT THE SEED TO THE REAL GREG PATH
+
+Inspect actual canonical module names and extend them. Suggested roles are contract types, capability-profile extensions, method adapters, eligibility/routing, typed receipts, verification, and evaluation. Suggested roles are not instructions to create duplicate directories.
+
+Integrate with:
+- MissionContract and ProblemGeometry;
+- Capability Genome and capability availability;
+- model routing and requested-versus-served provenance;
+- existing Task Fabric, Worker Leases, evaluator, and orchestration contracts;
+- durable events and institutional memory;
+- existing Consequence Gate and authenticated authority;
+- existing founder-correction and outcome-learning infrastructure;
+- Foundry and CapabilityDeficit handling.

+Reuse OMNIMORPH only when organizational composition improves the mission. A function call, deterministic workflow, or single worker should win whenever sufficient.
+
+Expose the result through the existing GREG interface: what problem was recognized, what method ran, why it was eligible, what evidence supports the answer, what remains uncertain, cost/time, and the next permitted step. Make this understandable on the phone and Chromebook. Do not expose implementation trivia as a prerequisite to normal use.

+DALEOBANKS may consume cognitive results for truthful research, multilingual explanation, and audience feedback. WealthMachine may consume them for estimation, venture evaluation, incentive analysis, and bounded optimization. Foundry may consume deficits and evaluated compositions. These are shared contracts; none becomes another GREG.

A media case can test truth-preserving paraphrase against source evidence; a venture case can test whether missing causal support prevents a confident revenue conclusion. Never publish, message others, spend, or activate live accounts solely to demonstrate integration.

+Complete a durable mission rehearsal through the actual runtime entry point: initiate, classify, execute heterogeneous computation, verify, persist, interrupt, restart, reconcile, inspect the receipt, and close or truthfully block. An isolated demo script is insufficient.

+Keep the project-wide operational bottleneck on the latest verified canonical path. The supplied snapshot's target is VEPMC 0 to 1 on the Chromebook. If it has changed, use the new evidence and record why.

+VEPMC requires the authorized mission on the intended body, durable state, actual capability use, respected approvals, interruption/restart recovery, no duplicate consequence, truthful closure/block, supporting evidence, and acceptance through the real authority path. A Linux container rehearsal, simulated browser, or per-test key cannot establish founder-device completion.

+# GREG bounded cognition
+
+GREG can now run structured mathematical and review tasks through its existing signed mission lifecycle. It selects an eligible specialized method, retains a typed receipt and proof, reobserves supported computations through the separate appraiser, and derives local competence and computational cell state from the canonical journal.
+
+Install the optional numerical dependencies and inspect or prepare a mission:
+
+```sh
+python -m pip install -r requirements-cognition.txt
+python -m greg cognition inventory
+python -m greg cognition mission --request examples/cognition/request.json --id m:exact --field output.exact --equals '"3"' --print-only
+```
+
+On an initialized and enrolled body, submit the ordinary mission with the existing founder key:
+
+```sh
+python -m greg cognition mission --request examples/cognition/request.json --id m:exact --field output.exact --equals '"3"' --key /path/to/founder.pem
+python -m greg run
+python -m greg cognition knowledge
+```
+
+The implementation includes 20 families: set-point micro rules; rational arithmetic and degree-at-most-four real polynomial roots; nonnegative product interval estimates; linear real-variable Z3 feasibility; bounded integer CP-SAT optimization; explicit graph and state search; Beta-Bernoulli updates; declared randomized differences in means; bounded PID; finite information value; seeded Bernoulli simulation; finite zero-sum minimax; protection review packets; population z-score anomalies; finite-horizon fully observed MDPs; local semantic interpretation; human review packets; independent-group quorums; and fixed-quadratic differential evolution. Every family has a declared scope and abstention boundary. Examples and the frozen assessment supply bounded inputs.
+
+`cognition.solve` compiles an explicit typed operation, checks dependency and registry eligibility, selects among eligible methods using appraised local competence and cost/latency estimates, executes a fixed reviewed worker, and checks the returned artifact. Unknown, detached, unavailable, expired, prohibited, unidentified, incomplete and high-consequence world-unverified requests abstain.
+
+`cognition.compose` performs one to four independent first passes within a shared declared budget. It preserves question identity, epistemic jurisdiction, assumptions and dissent. It does not vote truth or claim a measured composition advantage.
+
+`cognition.knowledge` returns current competence and bounded cell state replayed from the existing journal. Cell identity and credit survive restart; later appraisal refutation removes current credit. Native producer witnesses must match a signed mission's sensor, exact input digest, method version and fully verified current appraisal before settlement can earn routing credit.
+
+Receipts distinguish supplied-model formal validity, empirical validity and legitimate authority. Empirical validity remains `WORLD_UNVERIFIED`; authority remains `EXISTING_KERNEL_GATE_REQUIRED`; `authority_created` is false. Supplied completeness and randomization flags are assumptions rather than independent findings. High-consequence requests cannot acquire action authority from solver success. Law, consent and rights constraints cannot be traded for upside. Oversized proof abstains so retained receipts preserve all proof bytes.
+
+Workers enforce bounded input/output, time, CPU and memory on supported POSIX hosts using the existing isolation mechanism. Supplied code is never evaluated. Numerical extras and bounded synthetic cases do not establish general cognition, calibrated real-world predictions, identified real-world causality, autonomous homeostasis, optimality beyond declared solver/model limits or an external product outcome. Compute limits are domain-specific ceilings; actual operations and energy are not generally measured.
+
+The semantic seam reuses the existing local-model client only when GREG's effective configuration explicitly selects an installed local Ollama model. Hosted-provider fallback is disabled. Live local inference and comparative LLM baselines were unavailable in the development environment; missing local model evidence abstains.
+
+This change adds capabilities to the existing manifests and genomes, signed inbox, Gate, body, appraiser and event journal. It creates no second service, identity, ledger or consequence authority. Existing detach, stop, pause and lifecycle controls apply. Rollback detaches the added capabilities and reverts the patch while retaining history.
+
+Run the focused checks and frozen assessment:
+
+```sh
+python -m pytest -q tests/unit/test_greg_cognition.py tests/integration/test_greg_cognition_mission.py
+python -m greg.cognition.benchmark
+```
+
+The frozen assessment contains 22 structured operation and abstention cases. It exits unsuccessfully on a contract failure. Comparative scoring requires callable baselines with compatible answer/abstention structure and reported cost. Without all required baselines and an acceptance/utility policy, superiority and cross-geometry regret remain unmeasured. Local evidence is in `tests/evidence/cognition-2026-09-30/verification.json`; GitHub CI is separate evidence.

+"""Frozen cross-geometry assessment. Missing LLM baselines never imply superiority."""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import time
+
+from .contracts import digest
+from .cortex import reason, registry_view
+
+
+SUITE = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "examples" / "cognition" / "frozen-suite.json"
+
+
+def score(receipt, case, *, require_method=True):
+    expected = case["expected"]
+    if (require_method and receipt.get("method") != expected["method"]) or receipt.get("abstention_state") != expected.get("state", "NONE"):
+        return False
+    output = receipt.get("output") or {}
+    return all(output.get(k) == v for k, v in expected.get("output", {}).items())
+
+
+def assess(*, suite=SUITE, baselines=None):
+    raw = json.loads(Path(suite).read_text())
+    registry, rows = registry_view(), []
+    baseline_rows = {name: [] for name in (baselines or {})}
+    for case in raw["cases"]:
+        receipt = reason(case["request"], registry=registry)
+        rows.append({"id": case["id"], "correct": score(receipt, case), "method": receipt["method"],
+                     "state": receipt["abstention_state"], "latency": receipt["latency"], "cost_usd": receipt["money_cost"]})
+        for name, baseline in (baselines or {}).items():
+            started = time.monotonic()
+            try:
+                answer = baseline(case["request"])
+                good = score(answer, case, require_method=False)
+            except Exception as exc:
+                good, answer = False, {"error": type(exc).__name__}
+            baseline_rows[name].append({"id": case["id"], "correct": good, "latency": time.monotonic() - started,
+                                        "cost_usd": answer.get("money_cost"), "authorship": answer.get("method")})
+    measured = (set(raw["baseline_required_for_superiority"]) <= set(baseline_rows) and
+                all(all(r["cost_usd"] is not None for r in b) for b in baseline_rows.values()))
+    return {"suite_digest": digest(raw), "cases": rows, "correct": sum(r["correct"] for r in rows), "total": len(rows),
+            "baselines": baseline_rows, "superiority_status": "COMPARISON_REQUIRES_PREDECLARED_ACCEPTANCE" if measured else "UNMEASURED",
+            "cross_geometry_regret": None, "characterization": {"responsiveness": "per-case measured latency",
+                "memory_depth": "canonical receipt/mission history; restart integration tested separately",
+                "prediction_horizon": "declared finite horizons only", "adaptability": "outcome-ranked eligible capabilities",
+                "persistence": "existing GREG body, separate integration evidence", "error_correction": "independent artifact falsification",
+                "problem_space": "bounded structured operations", "cooperation": "typed composition; measured lift unproven",
+                "generalization": "unproven beyond this frozen corpus", "higher_scale_coherence": "unmeasured"},
+            "limits": "Structured inputs; local deterministic/math proof. No live LLM comparison, arbitrary-language classification, external outcome or VEPMC increment."}
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    report = assess()
+    print(json.dumps(report, indent=2, allow_nan=False))
+    raise SystemExit(0 if report["correct"] == report["total"] else 1)
